title: Exact linear descent of coefficient equivalences and mixed pullback comparisons
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]; such schemes are called allowed. For each finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the framework integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^s(T)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the PBC integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^p(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category].
For each allowed scheme $W$, suppose given exact $E$-linear equivalences $J_{W,E}:\mathcal C_E^s(W)\simeq\mathcal C_E^p(W)$ and exact natural scalar comparisons $j_{W,L/E}:J_{W,L}S_{L/E}\simeq P_{L/E}J_{W,E}$. Here $S,P$ and their associators $a^s,a^p$ are the actual transitions of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition, prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Assume the identity normalization, compatibility with shifts and the scalar cocycle
$$a^p_{M,L,E}\circ P_{M/L}(j_{W,L/E})\circ j_{W,M/L,S_{L/E}K}=j_{W,M/E}\circ J_{W,M}(a^s_{M,L,E}).$$
On the literal pair categories $\mathcal C_W$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and $\mathcal P_W$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], the formulas
$$J_W(E,K)=(E,J_{W,E}K),\qquad J_W[L,u]=[L,j_{W,L/F,H}\circ J_{W,L}(u)\circ j_{W,L/E,K}^{-1}]$$
for $u:S_{L/E}K\to S_{L/F}H$ define exact $\Omega$-linear equivalences. At every common stage this conjugation is a Hom bijection commuting with further scalar transport, and it and its inverse descend to inverse Hom-colimit maps. The functors preserve finite-stage inclusions, shifts and common-stage distinguished triangles in both directions, with no Karoubi completion.
Suppose additionally that for each allowed scheme isomorphism $h:U\simeq T$ there are natural finite rational comparisons $b_{h,E}:J_{U,E}F^s_{h,E}\simeq F^p_{h,E}J_{T,E}$ of the actual pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Assume their mixed scalar square, namely
$$F^p_{h,L}(j_T)\circ b_{h,L,S_TK}\circ J_{U,L}(\alpha^s_K)=\alpha^p_{J_{T,E}K}\circ P_U(b_{h,E,K})\circ j_{U,F^s_{h,E}K},$$
where $\alpha^s:S_UF^s_{h,E}\to F^s_{h,L}S_T$ and $\alpha^p:P_UF^p_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,L}P_T$ are the specified rational scalar/pullback comparisons. Then the finite-stage classes of $b_{h,E,K}$ define natural isomorphisms $b_h:J_UF_h^s\simeq F_h^pJ_T$ for the actual common-stage pullbacks. Any identity, composition, shift and scalar equations satisfied by the finite $b$ hold for these descended comparisons. When the finite equivalences and comparisons have the normalized integral lifts, these constructions supply precisely the common-stage fields of [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum, def-fd-pullback-comparison-datum].

proof.text: Fix $W$ and suppress it from the notation. All coefficient fields are subfields of the fixed $\Omega$; the index and each overfield index are small directed sets, since a compositum is a finite common overfield. The literal pair constructions in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] use the same index. Apply the additive pair-functor lemma [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] with $U=S$, $V=P$, $\Phi_E=J_E$, and its comparison $b_{L/E}=j_{L/E}^{-1}$. Inverting the stated scalar cocycle gives precisely that lemma's tower equation; identity normalization supplies its unit condition. It yields the functor on literal pairs with exactly the object and conjugation formulas in the statement. Only its pair-category conclusion is used, before its optional Karoubi extension.

proof.text:
Here is the transport calculation, including the associators. For endpoints $X=(E,K)$ and $Y=(F,H)$ put $r_X=j_{M/E,K}$, $t_X=j_{N/M,S_{M/E}K}$, $s_X=j_{N/E,K}$, $A_X=a^s_{N,M,E,K}$, $B_X=a^p_{N,M,E,J_EK}$, and use the analogous symbols for $Y$. The scalar cocycle says $s_XJ_N(A_X)=B_XP_{N/M}(r_X)t_X$. Write $\phi_M(u)=r_YJ_M(u)r_X^{-1}$. Since $u_N=A_YS_{N/M}(u)A_X^{-1}$, substitution gives
$$\phi_N(u_N)=B_YP(r_Y)t_YJ_N(Su)t_X^{-1}P(r_X)^{-1}B_X^{-1}=B_YP(\phi_M(u))B_X^{-1}=(\phi_M(u))_N.$$
The middle equality is naturality of $j_{N/M}$ at $u$. This proves the asserted commuting square on actual Hom transition maps, rather than on abstractly identified Hom groups.

proof.text:
At a fixed common field $M$, $J_M$ is fully faithful by the assumed equivalence, and conjugation by $r_X,r_Y$ is invertible. Thus $\phi_M$ is a bijection with inverse
$$\psi_M(v)=(J_M|_{\operatorname{Hom}})^{-1}(r_Y^{-1}vr_X).$$
The preceding transport identity and injectivity of $\phi_N$ give $\psi_N(v_N)=\psi_M(v)_N$. Therefore both maps respect eventual equality of representatives, the equality relation in the two pair categories. They descend to maps $[M,u]\mapsto[M,\phi_M(u)]$ and $[M,v]\mapsto[M,\psi_M(v)]$ on the two Hom colimits. Their composites are the identity on every representative. This proves both full faithfulness and the claimed inverse Hom-colimit maps without assuming any transition functor is faithful.

proof.text: For any target pair $(E,A)$, choose $K\in\mathcal C^s_E(W)$ and a finite-stage isomorphism $J_EK\simeq A$ using essential surjectivity of $J_E$. Its class at $E$, with inverse represented by the inverse finite map, is an isomorphism $J_W(E,K)\simeq(E,A)$. Together with the preceding Hom bijections, [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] now makes $J_W$ an equivalence (take a common sufficiently large universe for both pair categories). The object choices and Hom inverses describe its quasi-inverse: choose such a preimage for each target pair and lift morphisms uniquely through the Hom bijections after conjugating by these chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Final sentence: comparison with the PBC coefficient category; explicit agent-written common-stage descent argument.

proof.text:
The functor is additive by step 1. For $\lambda\in\Omega$ and $f=[M,u]$, choose a finite $N$ containing $M$ and $\lambda$. The scalar action on both pair categories is represented by $\lambda u_N$. Since $J_N$ is $N$-linear and composition in its target is bilinear,
$$\phi_N(\lambda u_N)=j_YJ_N(\lambda u_N)j_X^{-1}=\lambda\phi_N(u_N).$$
Step 2 identifies this with the transport of $\phi_M(u)$, so $J_W(\lambda f)=\lambda J_W(f)$. The inverse Hom bijections are also $\Omega$-linear: apply the injective linear map $J_W$ to the proposed additive and scalar identities. Conjugating these inverse Hom maps by the chosen object isomorphisms preserves linearity, so the quasi-inverse is linear too.

proof.text: At stage $E$, the identity comparison $j_{E/E}=1$ makes $J_W\iota^s_E=\iota^p_EJ_E$ on objects and arrows. Let $\delta_E:J_E(-[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(J_E-)[1]$ be the given exact-functor shift comparison. Compatibility of $j$ with shifts is exactly the transformation-compatibility equation for the families $J_E\circ[1]$ and $[1]\circ J_E$. Apply the compatible-transformation clause of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent]: the classes $[E,\delta_{E,K}]$ give the shift comparison of $J_W$, with inverse given by their inverse classes. Thus the comparison restricts to the specified finite-stage comparison, for the actual pair shifts.

proof.text: A distinguished source triangle is isomorphic to the inclusion of a distinguished triangle $D$ over a finite field $M$, by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Step 6 identifies its image with the inclusion of $J_M(D)$ using the given shift comparison. The assumed exactness of $J_M$ makes this triangle distinguished, so the target definition [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], whose distinguished triangles are those isomorphic to the common-stage cone triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] (with $T_{M/M}=\operatorname{id}$, a stage-$M$ distinguished triangle is its own cone triangle there), shows that $J_W$ preserves distinguished triangles. This proves exactness directly on the raw pair categories.

source.place: Final sentence: comparison with the PBC coefficient category; explicit agent-written common-stage descent argument.

proof.text: Conversely, let a triangle $D$ in the source have distinguished image. In the target pair category choose a finite-stage distinguished triangle $A$ and an isomorphism $J_WD\simeq\iota^p_M A$: by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] $J_WD$ is isomorphic to a common-stage cone triangle of some $[M,u]$, and the classes $[M,\operatorname{id}]:(E,K)\simeq(M,T_{M/E}K)$ identify that triangle with $\iota^p_M$ of the stage-$M$ cone triangle of $u$, the third arrow by the shift comparison $\sigma_{M/E}$. Choose an exact quasi-inverse $R_M$ of the assumed exact equivalence $J_M$. Then $R_M A$ is distinguished, and $J_MR_M A\simeq A$ as triangles, with the exact-equivalence shift comparisons. Using step 6 gives $J_W\iota^s_M R_M A\simeq J_WD$. Lift the three component isomorphisms and their inverses through the Hom bijections of step 3. Faithfulness, together with the shift comparison, lifts all triangle commutativity equations and the inverse identities. Hence $D\simeq\iota^s_M R_M A$, so $D$ is distinguished by the source definition. Applying this to the chosen quasi-inverse proves reverse exactness. This argument uses only finite-stage exact equivalences already assumed, and never a Karoubi completion.

proof.text:
Fix $h:U\simeq T$. To compare the actual composites, set $A_E=J_{U,E}F^s_{h,E}$ and $B_E=F^p_{h,E}J_{T,E}$. In the orientation required by the pair-functor lemma their scalar comparisons are
$$a_{L/E}=J_{U,L}(\alpha^s)\circ j_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}^{-1},\qquad c_{L/E}=F^p_{h,L}(j_T)^{-1}\circ\alpha^p_{J_{T,E}K}.$$
Indeed both start with $P_{U,L/E}$ applied to the stage-$E$ composite and end with the stage-$L$ composite applied to $S_{T,L/E}$. The actual source pullback representative formula is specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the target scalar/pullback comparisons and their unit and tower equations are specified in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and the actual target common-stage pullback $F^p_h$ is by [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] the functor descended from $(F^p_{h,E},\alpha^p)$ by the same conjugation formula $[M,u]\mapsto[M,(\alpha^p)^{-1}F^p_{h,M}(u)\alpha^p]$ as in the pair-functor lemma. Together with the assumed $j$ cocycle these give the composite stage families. The composition clause of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] identifies their descended functors with the actual $J_UF_h^s$ and $F_h^pJ_T$, respectively.

proof.text:
Multiply the assumed mixed scalar square on the left by $F^p_{h,L}(j_T)^{-1}$ and on the right by $j_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}^{-1}$. With the comparisons just defined, it becomes
$$b_{h,L,S_TK}\circ a_{L/E}=c_{L/E}\circ P_U(b_{h,E,K}).$$
This is exactly the compatible-transformation hypothesis of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent], so the components $[E,b_{h,E,K}]$ define a natural transformation $b_h:A\Rightarrow B$. Each is invertible: $[E,b_{h,E,K}^{-1}]$ is its two-sided inverse since the composites are represented by the finite identity maps. Thus it is a natural isomorphism with precisely the claimed components.

source.place: Final sentence: comparison with the PBC coefficient category; explicit agent-written common-stage descent argument.

proof.text:
For completeness, the naturality calculation uses the mixed square at both endpoints, not only at objects with field label $L$. For $u:S_{T,M/E}K\to S_{T,M/F}H$, suppress $h$ and write $a_E,c_E,a_F,c_F$ for the stage-$M$ comparisons. The representative of $B[u]\circ b_{E,K}$ is
$$c_F^{-1}B_M(u)c_EP_U(b_{E,K})=c_F^{-1}B_M(u)b_{M,S_EK}a_E=c_F^{-1}b_{M,S_FH}A_M(u)a_E=P_U(b_{F,H})a_F^{-1}A_M(u)a_E.$$
The middle equality is finite-stage naturality of $b_M$; the first and last use step 10. The last expression represents $b_{F,H}\circ A[u]$. Equality of these representatives proves naturality for arbitrary common-stage arrows.

proof.text: The identity and composition clauses of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] preserve composite stage families and equations of compatible transformations. Apply them to each finite identity or composition equation for $b$, retaining the actual pullback associators. Shift equations are equations of the shift comparisons descended in step 6, and scalar equations use the same compatible transformations and the scalar calculation of step 5. Thus every equation stipulated in the question descends; no new finite equation is being asserted. Finally [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum] asks, at common stage, for the field-preserving conjugation functor, its linearity, exactness in both directions and its induced shift comparisons, all proved in steps 1–8. [def-fd-pullback-comparison-datum] asks for the common-stage transformation of the two actual composites, with its prescribed finite components and mixed square, proved in steps 9–11. Under the stipulated normalized integral and finite rational data these supply exactly those common-stage fields; this does not construct the integral lifts.
